summary: ppa-builder stub exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and import
details: The package ships a stub whose `main` is a Proxy returning no-op functions for any property, and whose only real behavior is to invoke `beacon.cjs`. The declared `postinstall` script runs `node beacon.cjs`, and the main module re-invokes `beacon.fire()` on `require()`, so the beacon fires both at `npm install` time and on every import. beacon.cjs collects `os.hostname()`, the install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and the node/npm version, and POSTs them over cleartext HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The destination is not a publisher-controlled domain, the package provides no real functionality to the installer, and the scoped name `@ppa-web-components/*` resembles a private-registry namespace consistent with a dependency-confusion reconnaissance beacon mapping internal install environments.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
